About Us Testers Admin Bounty Hunters Interns Contact Contact Us Email Sign-Up Services All Services Red Teaming PCI QSA Projects/Tools All Tools RITA Other Fun Stuff Blog Webcasts Podcasts Events All Events Wild West Hackin\xe2\x80\x99 Fest 30 Oct 2015 Password Spray, Red Team password spraying, RPCCLINET Password Spraying & Other Fun with RPCCLIENT Joff Thyer // \xc2 Many of us in the penetration testing community ar\xe2\x80\x8be used to scenarios whereby we land a targeted phishing campaign within a Windows enterprise environment and have that wonderful access into the world of Windows command line networking tools.\xc2 \xc2 \xc2 You get your shell and before you know it, you are ready to run all your favorite enumeration commands.\xc2 \xc2 These are things like: C:\\> NET VIEW /DOMAIN C:\\> NET GROUP \xe2\x80\x9cDomain Administrators\xe2\x80\x9d /DOMAIN and so on.\xc2 \xc2 Not to mention that you often have all of the wealth of Metasploit post exploitation modules, and the many wonders of various PowerShell tools such as Veil, and PowerShell Empire. Imagine a world where all you have is a Linux host available on an internal network with no backdoor shell access to any existing Windows system.\xc2 \xc2 \xc2 Imagine that world wherein you are effectively segmented away from the rest of the network and cannot even capture useful network traffic using interception techniques such as Ettercap.\xc2 \xc2 This was indeed the case for me recently whereby all I could do was SSH into a single Linux host I controlled. After having not been in this situation in some time, I paused a moment before recalling the wonderful world of Samba. \xc2 In particular there are two excellent, and useful programs in the Samba suite namely \xe2\x80\x9crpcclient\xe2\x80\x9d, and its friend \xe2\x80\x9csmbclient\xe2\x80\x9d.\xc2 \xc2 Also, let us not forget our favorite DNS utility called \xe2\x80\x9cdig\xe2\x80\x9d. My first task was to use available reconnaissance to make informed guesses as to what the internal domain name was likely to be. \xc2 There are a few different methods to think about here but the first thing was to play with \xe2\x80\x9cdig\xe2\x80\x9d to determine DNS information of use.\xc2 \xc2 \xc2 I can try to look up the Windows global catalog record, and authoritative domain server records to determine domain controller addresses.\xc2 \xc2 Examples as follows: \xe2\x80\x8bThis will only give me answers if I have predicted or determined the correct \xe2\x80\x9cdomain.corp\xe2\x80\x9d name. Now, luckily for me I had access to internal Nessus vulnerability report data and had determined that SMB NULL sessions were permitted to some hosts.\xc2 \xc2 I matched up the data to my dig results and determined that the NULL sessions were actually corresponding to domain controller addresses.\xc2 \xc2 My next task was to try and enumerate user and group information from the domain controllers with \xe2\x80\x9crpcclient\xe2\x80\x9d only available to me.\xc2 \xc2 I quickly determined by using the \xe2\x80\x9cman\xe2\x80\x9d page that rpcclient could indeed perform an anonymous bind as follows:\xe2\x80\x8b \xe2\x80\x8bwhereby 10.10.10.10 was the chosen address of the domain controller I could anonymously bind to.\xc2 \xc2 After that command was run, \xe2\x80\x9crpcclient\xe2\x80\x9d will give you the most excellent \xe2\x80\x9crpcclient> \xe2\x80\x9d prompt.\xc2 \xc2 At this point in time, if you can use anonymous sessions, then there are some very useful commands within the tool.\xc2 1. Enumerate Domain Users 2. Enumerate Domain Groups 3.\xc2 Query Group Information and Group Membership 4. Query Specific User Information (including computers) by RID.\xe2\x80\x8b So in working with these basic commands, I was able to survey the landscape of Windows domain user, and group information pretty thoroughly. Another technique often used during a penetration test is called \xe2\x80\x9cPassword Spraying\xe2\x80\x9d.\xc2 This is a particularly effective technique whereby given a list of domain users, and knowledge of very common password use, the tester attempts to perform a login for every user in the list. \xc2 The technique is very effective given that you deliberately limit the list of passwords to try to a small number. \xc2 In fact a single password per spraying attempt is advisable for the sole reason that you really do not want to lock accounts. Before password spraying, it is very useful to determine the Windows domain password policy using a command such as \xe2\x80\x9cNET ACCOUNTS /DOMAIN\xe2\x80\x9d in the Windows world.\xc2 \xc2 However given that we don\xe2\x80\x99t have a Windows shell available to us, rpcclient gives us the following options. \xe2\x80\x8bAt least we are able to determine the crucial information about the password length.\xc2 After I write this, I will probably work out how to decode the password properties and match them back to the appropriate information but I have not yet done that task. In order to perform a password spray attack, the next step is to pick a common password (such as \xe2\x80\x9cAutumn2015\xe2\x80\x9d) and work out our technique on how to spray using \xe2\x80\x9crpcclient\xe2\x80\x9d.\xc2 \xc2 Conveniently, \xe2\x80\x9crpcclient\xe2\x80\x9d allows us to specify some commands on the command line which is very handy.\xc2 \xc2 \xc2 The follow two examples show a successful logon versus a failed logon.\xc2 (password of \xe2\x80\x9cbbb\xe2\x80\x9d is the correct logon) In these examples, we specifically told \xe2\x80\x9crpcclient\xe2\x80\x9d to run two commands, these being \xe2\x80\x9cgetusername\xe2\x80\x9d and then \xe2\x80\x9cquit\xe2\x80\x9d to exit out of the client.\xc2 \xc2 Now we have all of the ingredients to perform a password spraying attack.\xc2 \xc2 All we need is a bourne/bash shell loop and we are off to the races.\xc2 \xc2 Example of a simple shell script or command line to spray given that the \xe2\x80\x9cenumdomusers\xe2\x80\x9d output is in the \xe2\x80\x9cdomain-users.txt\xe2\x80\x9d file would be as follows. You know that you are successful when you see the string \xe2\x80\x9cAuthority\xe2\x80\x9d appear in the output.\xc2 \xc2 Lack of success for each user is going to be the \xe2\x80\x9cNT_STATUS_LOGON_FAILURE\xe2\x80\x9d message. If you begin to get the \xe2\x80\x9cACCOUNT_LOCKED\xe2\x80\x9d failure you should immediately stop your spray because you have likely sprayed too many times in a short period of time.
